claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is the environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service that specifies the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API.
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes aren't registered.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN can be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN, so a separate DNS record/domain is not required for the Terraform-compatible API.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN.

The state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the Terraform-compatible API domain in its terraform login / tofu login commands, TF_TOKEN_* variable name, and configuration.
The TF_TOKEN_* environment variable name for Terraform/OpenTofu credentials incorporates the backend domain, so it must use the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value for self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
A page exists at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/ documenting the Terraform state backend.
